summary: The patch rewrites SSTable.delete() in src/java/org/apache/cassandra/io/sstable/SSTable.java. It stats every component once, sorts the components by lastModified ascending, and deletes them in that order. DATA is no longer deleted first and SUMMARY is no longer deleted last. Each file is now removed with FileUtils.delete(String), not FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm. I applied the checklist file refdir/.claude/skills/shallow-review/references/general/specialists/resources.md and checked serialization, mixed-version, crash-safety and logging concerns. Nothing in the patch changes a serialized or on-disk format. Not reviewed: nothing. I found two problems. The caller still deletes DATA first, so the ordering fix is incomplete. And delete failures are now swallowed, which breaks the caller's retry logic.

findings.rule: IO and crash safety: error handling that swallows a disk failure; resource handling must still fail loudly
findings.problem: The patch replaces FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which throws FSWriteError, with FileUtils.delete(String), which calls File.delete() and ignores the boolean result. The only caller, LogTransaction.SSTableTidier.run() (LogTransaction.java:~401), relies on SSTable.delete() throwing. Its catch block logs 'Failed deletion', adds the tidier to failedDeletions and returns without releasing the parent ref. Now suppose Files.delete fails on any non-DATA component (EACCES, EIO, a read-only mount or a busy file). SSTable.delete() still returns true. The tidier then decrements totalDiskSpaceUsed, calls parentRef.release() and lets the txn log be cleaned up. The orphaned component files stay on disk. No error is logged and nothing retries. At next startup the txn log is gone, so the leftover files may be treated as a partial sstable, or they leak disk space permanently. This is a regression: before the patch a failed delete of any non-SUMMARY component raised and was retried.
findings.fix: Keep deleteWithConfirm for every component except SUMMARY. SUMMARY can use the non-confirming delete, as before. Leave the sort as is, but stay in sorted order and surface failures.

findings.rule: Crash safety: write/delete order must keep the REMOVE record's last-update-time invariant after a partial delete
findings.problem: The fix is incomplete. SSTableTidier.run() in LogTransaction.java (~lines 392-398) deletes the DATA file itself, via delete(datafile), before it calls SSTable.delete(). The sorted deletion therefore only covers the remaining components. If DATA is the newest non-STATS file (it was written or touched last, or timestamps tie or come out in an unusual order), the tidier deletes it first. A crash right after that leaves the other files on disk with an older max modification time than the REMOVE record holds. On restart LogFile.verifyRecord() reports 'last update time should have been ...' and the node refuses to start. This is the exact failure CASSANDRA-21649 describes. It is only avoided when DATA happens to be among the oldest files.
findings.fix: Remove the DATA-first special case in SSTableTidier.run(). Let SSTable.delete() own the order. If the tidier needs to know the DATA delete succeeded (the retry-later mechanism), have SSTable.delete() throw on failure, as in pc-1.
